items.claim: A parsed document that returned 200 with a defined entity reflected in the output is not an XXE finding; the entity may have been expanded from the document's own internal DTD, which is normal XML processing, and the flaw requires the parser to resolve a reference to an external resource or a local file.
items.disproof: The rule is wrong when the reflected value could only have come from outside the submitted document — a system property, a well-known file path, or a uniquely identifying marker the tester planted out of band — because then the internal-definition explanation is excluded and an external resolution actually occurred.

sources.quote: This also involves an attack that reads local files from the server, as XML entities can be defined to expand into the content of external resources.

The injected XML parser(s) could then bypass the limits imposed on XML external entities and/or have visibility of the XML files processed for other web applications deployed on the same Tomcat instance.

items.body: Mechanism: A parsed document that returned 200 with a defined entity reflected in the output is not an XXE finding; the entity may have been expanded from the document's own internal DTD, which is normal XML processing, and the flaw requires the parser to resolve a reference to an external resource or a local file. How to apply it in the field: treat this as the fp_rule it is — a hunter must be able to state the concrete observation that demonstrates it, with a request and response in hand, before the finding is reportable. Boundary of the rule: The rule is wrong when the reflected value could only have come from outside the submitted document — a system property, a well-known file path, or a uniquely identifying marker the tester planted out of band — because then the internal-definition explanation is excluded and an external resolution actually occurred.

items.claim: An XXE is proved by the parser resolving an external reference to a resource the submitted document never contained — a request the server issued to an attacker-controlled listener, or file content appearing that only exists on the host — because that is the observable effect entity resolution causes.
items.disproof: The claim is false when the environment blocks resolution so the payload produces a silent parse error or empty result with no outbound request; in that case the finding is a configuration weakness established by the parser defaults rather than a live XXE, and it must be reported as such instead of as a demonstrated read.

sources.quote: no_network - prevent network access when looking up external documents (on by default)
To disable entity expansion, use an XML parser that is configured with the option resolve_entities=False .
Use libxml_disable_entity_loader() to restrict loading of external files.

items.body: Mechanism: An XXE is proved by the parser resolving an external reference to a resource the submitted document never contained — a request the server issued to an attacker-controlled listener, or file content appearing that only exists on the host — because that is the observable effect entity resolution causes. How to apply it in the field: treat this as the validation it is — a hunter must be able to state the concrete observation that demonstrates it, with a request and response in hand, before the finding is reportable. Boundary of the rule: The claim is false when the environment blocks resolution so the payload produces a silent parse error or empty result with no outbound request; in that case the finding is a configuration weakness established by the parser defaults rather than a live XXE, and it must be reported as such instead of as a demonstrated read.

items.claim: A parser configured with network access disabled is not thereby safe against XXE, because a file:// or relative entity reference needs no network and the local-file read is the higher-value impact; a tester who stops at the network probe will miss it.
items.disproof: The rule is wrong when entity resolution is disabled outright — not merely network-restricted — because with resolve_entities off the external entity is never substituted and neither local nor remote disclosure is possible; the network flag alone is the insufficient control, the resolution flag is the effective one.

Use libxml_disable_entity_loader() to restrict loading of external files.

items.claim: Configuring the entity policy on the application's own XML parser call does not cover the parsers a framework or container instantiate internally for XSLT, tag library descriptors, JSP documents or configuration files, so those secondary parsers can bypass the entity limits the application believes it set.
items.disproof: The rule is false when the framework's internal parsers are the same configured object the application controls, or when the container or library applies a process-wide default that the application cannot override in either direction; then there is only one parser and the endpoint-level configuration does govern it.

sources.quote: In limited circumstances it was possible for a malicious web application to replace the XML parsers used by Tomcat to process XSLTs for the default servlet, JSP documents, tag library descriptors (TLDs) and tag plugin configuration files.

Boundary of the rule: The rule is false when the framework's internal parsers are the same configured object the application controls, or when the container or library applies a process-wide default that the application cannot override in either direction; then there is only one parser and the endpoint-level configuration does govern it.

items.claim: The standard that hardened against this class states the expected safe behaviour directly — entity references are disallowed in the XML stream — which gives the tester a concrete baseline for deciding whether a parser's default is safe rather than an opinion about what looks dangerous.
items.disproof: The claim is false when the surrounding protocol genuinely requires entity references for its correctness, because a parser that honours the disallow rule would break interoperability and the application must accept the risk in a narrower form; the baseline then applies to the untrusted-data boundary only, not to the whole document.

sources.quote: Consequently, version 1.2 of the SOAP standard explicitly disallows entity references in the XML stream.

In limited circumstances it was possible for a malicious web application to replace the XML parsers used by Tomcat to process XSLTs for the default servlet, JSP documents, tag library descriptors (TLDs) and tag plugin configuration files.
